governingStatute: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006 read with Income-tax Act, 1961 Section 43B(h)
statutorySection: Sections 15 & 16 of MSMED Act, 2006 read with Section 43B(h) of IT Act, 1961
title: Statutory payment timelines to Micro & Small Enterprises, compound penal interest, and income tax deduction disallowance

effectivePeriod.sunsetNotes: Section 43B(h) takes effect from FY 2023-24 (AY 2024-25) and continues under Section 37(2)(g) of the Income-tax Act, 2025.

plainTextSummary: Distinct legal mechanisms governing delayed payments to micro and small enterprises: (1) MSMED Act, 2006 Payment Mandate (Section 15): A buyer must pay a registered micro or small enterprise supplier on or before the agreed date in writing (which cannot exceed 45 days), or if no written agreement exists, before the 'appointed day' (15 days from physical delivery or removal of defects). (2) MSMED Act Compound Penal Interest (Sections 16 & 23): Failure to pay on time incurs mandatory compound interest with monthly rests at 3 times the RBI Bank Rate from the due date until actual payment. Under Section 23 of the MSMED Act, this interest is strictly non-deductible in computing taxable income. (3) Income-tax Act Accrual Disallowance (Section 43B(h) / Act 2025 Section 37(2)(g)): If payment to a micro or small enterprise is not made within the Section 15 timeline, the underlying invoice expenditure is disallowed in the financial year of incurrence and allowed only in the year of actual payment; the proviso allowing payment up to the tax return due date (Section 139(1)) does not apply to clause (h). (4) Trader Exclusion: Per Ministry of MSME OM dated 2 July 2021 and RBI Circular FIDD.MSME & NFS.BC.No.13/06.02.31/2021-22, retail and wholesale traders (NIC 45, 46, 47) are eligible for Udyam solely for Priority Sector Lending; they are excluded from Chapter V (Sections 15-25) of the MSMED Act and are therefore exempt from Section 43B(h) tax disallowance.

keyStatutoryThresholds.penalInterestRate: 3 times the Bank Rate notified by the Reserve Bank of India (compounded monthly)
keyStatutoryThresholds.statutoryInterestDisallowance: Section 23 of MSMED Act prohibits claiming Section 16 penal interest as an income tax deduction
keyStatutoryThresholds.taxAccrualDisallowanceSection43Bh: Disallows deduction of overdue principal in year of incurrence; allowed strictly upon payment under Section 43B(h) / Act 2025 Section 37(2)(g)
keyStatutoryThresholds.applicableEnterprises: Micro and Small Enterprises with valid Udyam Registration (Medium Enterprises are excluded from Chapter V)
keyStatutoryThresholds.traderExclusionRule: Enterprises registered solely under Retail and Wholesale Trade (NIC Codes 45, 46, 47) are excluded from delayed payment benefits per Ministry of MSME OM No. 5/2(2)/2021-E/P & G/Policy and RBI Circular FIDD.MSME & NFS.BC.No.13/06.02.31/2021-22
keyStatutoryThresholds.disputeStatutoryBasis: Explanation (b) to Section 2(n) of MSMED Act: buyer must lodge written objection regarding defects within 15 days of delivery to prevent deemed acceptance

requiredDocumentChecklist: Supplier Udyam Registration Certificate verifying classification (Micro or Small)
Udyam National Industry Classification (NIC) 2-digit/4-digit code check (Confirm not retail/wholesale trader)
Purchase Order / Written Agreement establishing payment term (Must not exceed 45 days)
Goods Receipt Note (GRN) or Service Acceptance record establishing the "appointed day"
Dispute record in writing filed within 15 days of delivery (if goods were defective or incomplete)
